q: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress held in Bombay in 1885?
exp: The first INC session (1885, Bombay) was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee; A. O. Hume was its founder-organiser.

q: Which is the longest river that flows entirely within India?
exp: The Ganga (about 2,525 km) is the longest river wholly in India; Brahmaputra and Indus rise outside India.

q: Which modern city of Bihar was the ancient Mauryan capital Pataliputra?
exp: Pataliputra, capital of the Magadha-Mauryan empire, is the modern city of Patna.

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
exp: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

q: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
exp: Electric charge is measured in coulomb (1 C = 1 A x 1 s); ampere is the unit of current.

q: The slogan 'Do or Die' was given by which leader during the Quit India Movement of 1942?
exp: Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, on 8 August 1942.

q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
exp: It passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram - 8 states.

q: The festival Chhath, widely celebrated in Bihar, is dedicated to which deity?
exp: Chhath Puja is a four-day festival in which the Sun god Surya and Chhathi Maiya are worshipped.

q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
exp: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee; Rajendra Prasad presided over the Constituent Assembly.

q:
Match the institution with its year of establishment.
P. Reserve Bank of India   Q. NABARD   R. Planning Commission
1. 1982   2. 1950   3. 1935
exp: RBI was set up in 1935, NABARD in 1982 and the Planning Commission in 1950.

q: Which of the following was among the first recipients of the Bharat Ratna in 1954?
exp: The 1954 awardees were C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan and C. V. Raman.

q: The Battle of Plassey, which laid the foundation of British rule in India, was fought in
exp: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between Robert Clive and Siraj-ud-Daulah.

q: Which is the highest peak lying entirely within India?
exp: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) is the highest peak in India; K2 and Everest are not wholly in India.

q: The famous Nalanda Mahavihara is traditionally believed to have been founded by which Gupta ruler?
exp: Nalanda was founded in the 5th century CE under Kumaragupta I; Dharmapala founded Vikramshila.

q: What is the minimum age required to be elected as the President of India?
exp: Article 58 requires a candidate to have completed 35 years of age.

q: Which gas forms the largest percentage of Earth's atmosphere by volume?
exp: Dry air contains about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

q: Who founded the Mauryan Empire in 322 BCE with the help of Kautilya?
exp: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nandas and founded the Maurya empire with Chanakya's guidance.

q:
Statement I: Rajasthan is the largest Indian state by area.
Statement II: Goa is the smallest Indian state by area.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
exp: Rajasthan (about 3.42 lakh sq km) is the largest state and Goa the smallest by area; both statements are true.

q: Madhubani painting is a traditional folk art of which region of Bihar?
exp: Madhubani (Mithila) painting originated in the Mithila region of north Bihar.

q: What is the term of a member of the Rajya Sabha?
exp: Rajya Sabha is a permanent house; each member serves a six-year term, with one-third retiring every two years.

q: Major Dhyan Chand, regarded as a legend of Indian sport, was associated with which game?
exp: Dhyan Chand won three Olympic golds (1928, 1932, 1936) in hockey; his birthday is National Sports Day.

q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre at Amritsar took place in
exp: General Dyer ordered firing on 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi day).

q: Chilika Lake, the largest brackish-water lagoon in India, is located in which state?
exp: Chilika Lake lies on the coast of Odisha along the Bay of Bengal.

q: Which river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because of its frequent floods?
exp: The Kosi shifts its course often and causes recurrent floods in north Bihar.

q: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by which Amendment?
exp: The 42nd Amendment (1976), on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation, added Part IV-A.

q: Which Mughal emperor built the Red Fort at Delhi?
exp: Shah Jahan built the Red Fort (Lal Qila) when he shifted the capital to Shahjahanabad (1639-48).

q: The black soil of the Deccan plateau is best suited for which crop?
exp: Regur (black) soil retains moisture and suits cotton, hence called 'black cotton soil'.

q: At which place did Gautama Buddha attain enlightenment?
exp: Siddhartha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya in Bihar.

q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right under Part III of the Constitution?
exp: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from Part III; it is now a legal right under Article 300A.

q:
Assertion (A): Sea water boils at a slightly higher temperature than pure water.
Reason (R): Dissolved salts raise the boiling point of a liquid.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
exp: Dissolved solutes lower vapour pressure and cause elevation of boiling point, so A is true and explained by R.

q: Who founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828?
exp: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha (Brahmo Samaj) in Calcutta in 1828.

q: The Sundarbans mangrove delta, home of the Royal Bengal Tiger, lies mainly in which Indian state?
exp: The Indian Sundarbans in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta lie in West Bengal.

q: Bihar was separated from the Bengal Presidency and formed into a separate province in
exp: Bihar and Orissa became a separate province in 1912; Bihar and Orissa were split in 1936.

q: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
exp: The 73rd Amendment (1992) added Part IX and the 11th Schedule; the 74th dealt with urban local bodies.

q: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
exp: Alexander Fleming noticed the antibacterial action of Penicillium mould in 1928.

q: Mother Teresa was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in which year?
exp: Mother Teresa received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her humanitarian work.

q: Who is the author of the book 'The Discovery of India'?
exp: Nehru wrote it in Ahmednagar Fort prison in 1944.

q: National Science Day in India is celebrated every year on
exp: It commemorates the discovery of the Raman Effect announced by C. V. Raman on 28 February 1928.

q: Which is the national animal of India?
exp: The Bengal tiger (Panthera tigris) is India's national animal.

q: Who was the first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold medal?
exp: Abhinav Bindra won gold in 10 m air rifle at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
